hints.title: Specifying Custom Date Patterns
hints.text: Use the date formatting function to transform calendar date records into full textual representation.

hints.title: Forming Format Specifiers
hints.text: Use %W for full weekday name, %M for month name, %e for day of the month without leading zero, and %Y for 4-digit year.

hints.title: Maintaining Column Aliases
hints.text: Assign the transformed expression the alias day matching the expected table schema.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(day, '%W, %M %e, %Y') AS day
FROM Days;
```

complexity.time: O(N) linear scan over date rows
complexity.notes: Direct string formatting of calendar dates.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: String concatenation of year, month, and day parts is verbose and error-prone.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Standard format specifiers execute in a single C-level format pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should know date formatting tokens like %W, %M, %e, and %Y.

solutions.code:
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(day, '%W, %M %e, %Y') AS day
FROM Days;

SELECT TRIM(TO_CHAR(day, 'FMDay, FMMonth FMDD, YYYY')) AS day
FROM Days;

import pandas as pd

def convert_date_format(days: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    # %e is day without leading zero, formatted manually or via strftime
    days["day"] = pd.to_datetime(days["day"]).apply(lambda d: f"{d.strftime('%A, %B')} {d.day}, {d.year}")
    return days
